This is the Hybrid RAG workbench, running live. On the Documents tab, I upload an HR policy PDF.
Ingestion runs as a background job. The text is split into chunks, embedded into a FAISS index, and a language model extracts facts for a knowledge graph.
Two pages became six chunks, and forty-eight graph facts.
Now I ask a question in plain English. Hybrid mode searches both indexes at the same time.
A NeMo guardrail screens the question first. Then retrieval runs, and G P T four o writes the answer.
The answer arrives with citations. C marks a passage from the PDF. K marks a fact from the knowledge graph. And both guardrails passed.
Below the answer is the evidence. FAISS ranked these passages by similarity. The knowledge graph linked entities from the question, and returned the exact facts it used.
How this answer was built: both guardrail checks, and the time each step took.
The Evaluation tab scores answers with DeepEval, using G P T four o as the judge. Faithfulness, relevancy, precision and recall all score one. Context relevancy is the next thing to tune.

Under the hood, each PDF is indexed twice: as vectors, and as a graph. Every question passes a guardrail, searches both, and fuses the evidence. G P T four o answers, and a second rail checks it is grounded.
Seventy-seven automated tests cover the pipeline. It runs on FastAPI, Streamlit, and Docker. Every answer, with its evidence.
